hypotheses.justification: This instance is not needed by the statement. A comparison argument replaces the totally complex integral formula. Put σ = s.re, d = [K:ℚ], m = #InfinitePlace K, x = idealSetElement K J a and N = idealSetIntNorm K J a ≥ 1. By the definitions of fundamentalCone and logMap and ZSpan.fundamentalDomain_isBounded, log(w x) − log(N)/d is uniformly bounded for every place except the distinguished one. InfinitePlace.prod_eq_abs_norm and sum_mult_eq give the same bound at that remaining place. Consequently P = ∏ w, (w x)^2 ≥ c N^(2m/d) ≥ c N for some c > 0 independent of a: multiplicities are 1 or 2, so d ≤ 2m. The instance-free lemmas norm_complexPlaceMellinGaussian and integral_totallyComplexGaussian_eq_prod express the integral as C P^(−σ), hence bound it by C c^(−σ) N^(−σ). Apply Summable.of_norm_bounded to the norm of summable_idealSet_inverseNormPower, which also needs no totally complex instance. All x are nonzero and N ≥ 1 by idealSetElement_ne_zero and idealSetIntNorm_ne_zero, so no zero/junk-value case arises. Number fields have positive degree and nonempty infinite places; the argument also covers unit rank zero.
